description: TEP distance kernel vs optimally-tuned conventional predictors (IDW, kNN, unconstrained GP) on the Step 34 leave-one-day-out folds

headline: On 318 leave-one-day-out folds, the TEP Gaussian kernel (lambda constrained to 1,000-10,000 km, form fixed by Papers 1-2 AIC) scores -0.1% relative to the training-selected conventional spatial predictor (inverse-distance weighting, k-NN, or an unconstrained Gaussian process; positive favours TEP), with 95% CI [-0.5, +0.0], and is positive on 43% of days. The tep_hybrid selector (TEP added to the training-day candidate set) scores +0.0% vs the conventional-only selector (CI [+0.0, +0.0], 8% of days), selecting TEP on 50/318 days. An unconstrained GP independently selects lambda ~ 1500 km and form gaussian (190/318 days). In the diagnostic band-passed gap segment the TEP kernel beats the causally selected temporal predictor by +64.7% (CI [+63.3, +66.8], 100% of days); this offline-filtered diagnostic is not a real-time proof.
